title: QBR - Orion Systems - Health & Usage Review
summary: Quarterly business review focusing on usage trends, rising costs due to tail latency and retries, reliability incidents in August, roadmap alignment for Dedicated pools and private VPC deployment, and next steps to run targeted benchmarks and share security/compliance artifacts.
topics: Usage and cost trends (token usage, embeddings)
Reliability incidents and mitigation (august outage, fallbacks)
Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and pilot timeline
Security & compliance requests (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs)
Performance tuning: batching, KV cache, quantization recommendations
Roadmap alignment and upcoming Redwood features
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-10-06 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Natarajan, Jordan Lee (Redwood)
Maya Patel, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Ramos (Orion Systems)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR, um, appreciate you blocking time. we wanted to cover the usage trends, cost drivers, reliability items, and then map the roadmap so we can align on the next quarter.
[00:12] Maya Patel: thanks Alex. thanks, Jordan, Priya. yes we got the agenda, should be good.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: quick note — we'll also cover security asks that came up in your ticket last month.
[00:24] Liam O'Connor: perfect, we have a few exec-level questions but mostly looking for concrete action items.
[00:30] Priya Natarajan: great. to start, I'll run through the usage dashboard we shared. so Orion's month-to-month token consumption dipped in July, spiked in August because of retry storms during that incident, and has normalized but at a 12% higher baseline than Q2.
[00:50] Priya Natarajan: the embedding calls are now about 30% of your token bill — mostly due to reprocessing of search indexes. there's also a small but consistent cost from long-context chat sessions since you increased the retention window.
[01:05] Sofia Ramos: yeah the re-index job we ran in August definitely contributed. we scheduled it during a maintenance window but retries piled up. is there a way to better throttle or batch those?
[01:14] Priya Natarajan: absolutely. batching at the application layer helps, and on our side we can suggest a batching window and recommend the continuous batching config. also enable prefix caching for repeated prompts — that'll cut the per-token cost for many of those calls.
[01:28] Maya Patel: when you say prefix cache, is that the KV cache you talked about in the docs? we've seen references to KV cash in one doc actually — typo.
[01:36] Priya Natarajan: yeah that's the KV cache, sometimes shows up as 'KV cash' in autogenerated docs, ha. it's the same — it stores key-value activations for recurring prefixes so you don't recompute. for your long chat flows it should help a lot.
[01:46] Alex Chen: quick add — we noticed a pattern where some retry policies at the client caused duplicate small requests rather than batching. our suggestion is to push retry backoff and add idempotency keys.
[01:56] Liam O'Connor: noted. on costs: could you send a breakdown of the spike? the finance team wants an itemized list to correlate to our internal deploys.
[02:03] Jordan Lee: we'll send a CSV and also the dashboard link. action item: Alex to share the month-by-month billing and the list of top endpoints by cost.
[02:11] Maya Patel: thanks. next, reliability: we had that outage on 2026-08-17, and our SREs reported increased tail latency near peak hours. can you summarize root cause?
[02:22] Priya Natarajan: yes, we investigated. during the peak window, a model fallback policy triggered multiple times because the primary model hit a kernel OOM on some long sequences; the smart routing attempted the next compatible variant but that increased cold-starts and queueing. combined with retries, that created a overload loop.
[02:43] Priya Natarajan: short version: kernel memory pressure + aggressive retry = tail latency spike.
[02:49] Sofia Ramos: memory pressure — was that a model issue or infra?
[02:53] Priya Natarajan: a mix. model sequence lengths were longer than typical, and the runtime chose a kernel path that wasn't optimal for that shape; we have a kernel selection fix in the pipeline. also, the fallback policy didn't prefer a smaller-quantized variant which would've been cheaper and faster.
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: what about Dedicated? would a dedicated GPU pool have avoided that?
[03:14] Alex Chen: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor interference and gives you reserved capacity, so you'd have more predictable latency. however, if the kernel/execution path is the wrong one for long sequences, it still impacts you — but it's easier to test and benchmark in Dedicated.
[03:28] Maya Patel: we're evaluating Dedicated for Q4. what's the typical ramp time?
[03:33] Jordan Lee: for a small pilot it's about 2-3 weeks from contract to capacity provisioning, then a week of validation and benchmarks. for full production it's usually 6-8 weeks depending on region and capacity commitments.
[03:45] Maya Patel: good to know.
[03:47] [04:00] Priya Natarajan: on the performance side, we'll propose a quantization profile — for many of your workloads, an int8 profile gives 2-3x throughput with minor quality delta. we can test this in a canary on Dedicated.
[04:18] Sofia Ramos: are there any model quality regressions we should expect? we have sensitive NLU tasks.
[04:23] Priya Natarajan: we'll include a small eval set you provide and run generation comparisons. if regression is noticeable, we can fallback to mixed precision or a different quant profile. and Redwood Optimize will track quality drift on your evals.
[04:39] Liam O'Connor: security: our compliance team asked for KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC 2 cert copy. where do those stand?
[04:47] Jordan Lee: SOC 2 Type II cert is in the portal — we'll share the link after the call. KMS support is available for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK via partner KMS in certain regions.
[05:02] Maya Patel: our requirement is customer-managed keys (BYOK) and immutable audit logs for models and inference requests. is that supported on Private only?
[05:11] Alex Chen: customer-managed keys + fully private control plane is supported on Private deployments. Dedicated can support KMS with some constraints depending on infrastructure. we'll detail this in the security brief.
[05:23] Sofia Ramos: also SSO and RBAC — we've got multiple teams and need role separation.
[05:28] Jordan Lee: SAML SSO and coarse RBAC is supported; fine-grained route-level access can be configured via our console. we'll add a doc link.
[05:38] [05:40] Priya Natarajan: next up, roadmap alignment. in November we're rolling out enhanced autoscaling policies and a new default kernel selector that reduces OOMs for long sequences. December has improved cost analytics with token-level lineage.
[05:56] Alex Chen: for Orion specifically, we want to prioritize the Dedicated pilot and the quantization experiment so you can see cost-per-request improvements before committing to a larger reserve.
[06:07] Maya Patel: timeline wise, we want results before holiday demo in mid-December. is that realistic?
[06:12] Priya Natarajan: yes — pilot in October, 2 weeks of benchmarks in Nov, and then optimizations through early Dec. we'll need your eval set and a representative traffic replay.
[06:24] Liam O'Connor: about traffic replay, what's the best format? we can export request logs but they have some PII.
[06:30] Jordan Lee: scrub sensitive fields, obfuscate user IDs, and provide payloads; we also accept sampling if the dataset is large. we'll sign an NDA for any raw logs if necessary.
[06:42] [07:00] Sofia Ramos: one more technical: we saw higher memory usage for the reranking model. is that because of attention window?
[07:07] Priya Natarajan: likely yes — reranking with cross-attention can be heavy. options: shorter context per candidate, use approximate rerank with embeddings followed by narrow re-rank, or switch to a quantized reranker.
[07:20] Maya Patel: can you prototype an embeddings-first rerank in the pilot?
[07:24] Priya Natarajan: yep, we can. that should drop memory and cost substantially.
[07:30] Alex Chen: quick commercial note — given the increased baseline usage, we'd recommend a small reserved commit for Dedicated to lower unit cost while still keeping some burst capacity.
[07:40] Liam O'Connor: what's the minimum commit?
[07:42] Jordan Lee: we have a flexible starter commit; I'll send the pricing sheet, but generally a one-month reserved baseline for a small pool is common in pilots.
[07:53] [08:00] Maya Patel: ok let's talk action items and owners.
[08:04] Jordan Lee: sure. action: Priya to run a 95th/99th percentile latency benchmark on a Dedicated pilot using your traffic replay by Oct 13.
[08:15] Priya Natarajan: noted. I'll need the replay and eval set by Oct 9.
[08:20] Alex Chen: action: Alex to send the month-by-month cost breakdown and top HTTP endpoints by cost today.
[08:26] Maya Patel: action: Maya to pull and redact the replay logs and provide eval set by Oct 9.
[08:32] Sofia Ramos: action: Sofia to prepare a list of compliance questions and circulate them.
[08:36] Liam O'Connor: we'll also need a short exec summary for finance.
[08:39] Alex Chen: we'll include that in the billing breakdown.
[08:43] [09:00] Priya Natarajan: any other blockers on Dedicated? network egress and region — where should we provision?
[09:09] Sofia Ramos: prefer us-east-1 for latency, but we can test in eu-west-1 for DR.
[09:15] Priya Natarajan: noted, we'll provision in us-east-1.
[09:19] Maya Patel: ok final question: how do we measure success post-pilot?
[09:23] Jordan Lee: agreed success metrics: 95th percentile latency improvement >20% over hosted baseline, cost-per-inference reduction >=25% for reranks/embeddings, and no production-quality regressions on your evals.
[09:36] Liam O'Connor: sounds good. set those as KPIs.
[09:40] Alex Chen: perfect. recap and next steps — we'll send the security brief, SOC2 link, pricing sheet, and schedule the Dedicated provision call.
[09:49] Maya Patel: thanks everyone. appreciate the clear plan.
[09:52] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and owners.
[09:56] Alex Chen: meeting adjourned.
next_steps: Send month-by-month billing and top endpoints by cost (Alex) — sent same day
Provision Dedicated pilot in us-east-1 and run benchmarks (Priya) — target Oct 13

Share SOC2 cert and security brief (Jordan) — within 2 business days
